note: Portable expectations from authored vectors and the documented 1.13c rules. Not yet bound to a ds1edit.contract/1 original-function reference: each assumption below needs an identified-original result before its value can be called game behaviour.

cases.rule: main=(cell>>20)&0x3F, sub=(cell>>8)&0xFF; walls by orientation, floors 0, shadows 13
non-key bits neither move the key nor are rewritten
prop1==0 -> no tile (bt_idx 0); no block -> -1; editor-disabled blocks skipped
editor policy, not a game rule

cases.note: ds1_read() applying the table is package C's reader test

cases.rule: 256 buckets by position, count + 160-byte records, bucket = uppercase byte sum & 0xFF, linear walk
editor promise: a .cof extension on the query is ignored
editor policy: ms = 10240 / speed (truncated), default when speed <= 0 or > 65535, capped at 10000
cases.note: kept separate from any game fixed-point claim

cases.rule: first 1024 bytes of .pl2 are 256 x (c0, c1, c2, pad); index 0 transparent; gamma per channel; < 1024 bytes -> grey ramp
LvlTypes act 1-5, else DS1 act 1-5, else act 1
shade c reads row 0x400 + (c/8)*256; short tables read nothing past their end

assumptions.assumed: PL2 base entry bytes are R, G, B, pad (editor's current reading)
assumptions.disputed_by: docs/guides/palettes-and-colour.md describes B, G, R, pad; the D2CMP 0x9d30 nearest-colour check is channel-order-agnostic and does not settle it
assumptions.evidence_needed: an original-game screenshot or framebuffer read of a known index (e.g. Act 3 index 230 ground, Act 1 index 98) with the identified 1.13c Pal.PL2 bytes

evidence.ref: d2-fleet member 10.0.10.30:8800 (lod-113c), in game in the Rogue Encampment, fleet_frame PNG sha256 559f0fb8a847f641230bb7b268146eec424d0b500a191fd5768c08a8a657b53c
evidence.observation: the frame's 256-entry palette equals the vanilla 1.13c Act1 Pal.pl2 base table read as (R,G,B,pad) at all 256 indices (as (B,G,R,pad): 43/256, only the grey/symmetric entries); 99.6% of frame pixels are exactly an Act1 entry read RGBX vs 15.8% read BGRX
the life orb is index 5, Pal.pl2 bytes 5C 00 00 00 (red if byte 0 is red); the mana orb is index 138, bytes 00 00 58 00 (blue if byte 2 is blue). The orbs are red and blue.
for every act, pal.dat read as (B,G,R) equals Pal.pl2 read as (R,G,B,pad) at 256/256 entries: pal.dat is the BGR file, the PL2 base table is RGB+pad

limitations: the member's palette matched the PL2 table exactly, so its in-game gamma was identity (or the capture reads the pre-gamma palette); gamma is not settled here
assumptions.artifacts: tmp/visual-diagnosis/pl2/ (local only: frame, extraction script, result)

assumptions.assumed: equal-distance nearest-colour candidates resolve to the lowest index; index 0 is never chosen
assumptions.evidence_needed: FindNearestPaletteColor (D2CMP 6fe19d30) tie behaviour on a palette with duplicate entries

evidence.observation: 51 captured vectors on the 'ties' palette have two or more equidistant candidates; all 51 answers are the lowest index

limitations: 'index 0 is never chosen' is the caller convention (entries = palette + 4, count 255) used by the capture; which callers pass that range is not established here

assumptions.assumed: stored record names compare case-insensitively (queries are uppercased by the game; stored names are uppercase in vanilla)
assumptions.evidence_needed: 6fd91d00 compare on a mixed-case stored name

evidence.observation: uppercases the query in place (a-z minus 0x20), sums its bytes into the bucket index, then walks 0xa0-byte records calling 6fd91d00
after <=8 length guards, returns *(int*)a == *(int*)b && a[1] == b[1]: an exact 8-byte compare, no case folding

assumptions.resolution: src/core/animdata.c now uppercases the query into a zero-padded 8-byte key and memcmp()s all 8 stored bytes (was strnicmp over strlen). Regression tests: test_stored_names_are_compared_exactly_after_uppercasing_the_query, test_bytes_after_the_stored_name_terminator_take_part. Vanilla data is unaffected (every stored name is upper-case and NUL-padded).
limitations: the bytes after the query terminator are assumed zero (the caller's buffer padding was not traced)
